title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
problem: Language model pretraining methods are hard to compare carefully because training is computationally expensive, often uses private datasets of different sizes, and final results are highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices.
It is challenging to determine which aspects of existing self-training methods contribute the most because tuning is limited by computational cost and training data varies in size across methods.
BERT was significantly undertrained, making later reported improvements difficult to interpret relative to training procedure and data effects.
Previously overlooked design choices raise questions about the source of recently reported improvements in post-BERT methods.
core_techniques: [1] training the model longer, with bigger batches, over more data | 더 오래, 더 큰 배치로, 더 많은 데이터에서 학습하는 절차
[1] removing the next sentence prediction objective | NSP 목적함수를 제거하는 방법
[1] training on longer sequences | 더 긴 시퀀스로 학습하는 방법
[1] dynamically changing the mask-ing pattern applied to the training data | 학습 데이터에 적용되는 마스킹 패턴을 동적으로 바꾸는 방법
[5] FULL-SENTENCES without NSP loss | NSP 손실 없이 FULL-SENTENCES 입력 형식을 사용하는 방법
[5] a larger byte-level BPE | 더 큰 byte-level BPE 어휘 체계
[1] CC-NEWS | 새로 수집한 대규모 뉴스 데이터셋을 추가하는 방법

contributions: [1] We present a set of important BERT design choices and training strategies and introduce alternatives that lead to better downstream task performance.
[1] We use a novel dataset, CC-NEWS, and confirm that using more data for pretraining further improves performance on downstream tasks.
[1] Our training improvements show that masked language model pretraining, under the right design choices, is competitive with all other recently published methods.
